title: VLRS-Bench: A Vision-Language Reasoning Benchmark for Remote Sensing
claim: A benchmark organizes complex reasoning into a hierarchy of dimensions and fine-grained tasks, each grounded in concrete example questions.
layout: Central radial taxonomy wheel with three arrows to surrounding example panels
description: A central concentric wheel carries the VLRS-Bench logo. Three inner sectors are Prediction (blue), Decision (green) and Cognition (orange). Outer rings split each into abilities and then into fourteen labeled tasks, each with a sample count such as [125] or [250]. Curved red arrows link three groups of tasks to example panels around the wheel. The top-left panel, on spatiotemporal predictive reasoning, shows a grid of time-series satellite images with a reference ground-truth image and a multiple-choice question. The bottom-left panel, on spatial decision reasoning, shows an annotated map with a question and one option. The right panel, on complex cognitive reasoning, shows two before/after aerial images, a long question, and options A to H. Key phrases are in red. The panels have soft blue, green and orange backgrounds that match the wheel sectors.
caption: Illustrative cases from VLRS-Bench. The benchmark comprises three core reasoning dimensions (Cognition Reasoning: Why is this; Decision Reasoning: How to do; Prediction Reasoning: What will happen), further decomposed into six specific abilities and fourteen fine-grained tasks for comprehensive evaluation of MLLM reasoning.
abstract: Recent advancements in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have enabled complex reasoning. However, existing remote sensing (RS) benchmarks remain heavily biased toward perception tasks, such as object recognition and scene classification. This limitation hinders the development of MLLMs for cognitively demanding RS applications. To address this, we propose a Vision Language ReaSoning Benchmark (VLRS-Bench), which is the first benchmark exclusively dedicated to complex RS reasoning. Structured across the three core dimensions of Cognition, Decision, and Prediction, VLRS-Bench comprises 2,000 question-answer pairs with an average question length of 129.87 words, spanning 14 tasks and up to eight temporal phases. VLRS-Bench is constructed via a specialized pipeline that integrates RS-specific priors and expert knowledge to ensure geospatial realism and reasoning complexity. Experimental results reveal significant bottlenecks in existing state-of-the-art MLLMs, providing critical insights for advancing multimodal reasoning within the remote sensing community.
